queue.title: F12 (severity A, open) - spec loop: an idle loop must not erase its own history
queue.detail: FULL SPEC LOOP: explore+propose -> review -> review -> implement, as four passes. F12, confirmed live and never fixed: `stop_when_queue_empties` defines empty by TERMINAL_FOR_BINDING = ('approved','rejected') (scheduler.py:91), so a loop whose agent finished every task is NOT empty - the tasks sit `completed` awaiting review. Measured: both tasks completed 17:56, the loop then fired 17:57/17:58/17:59, once a minute, stopping only at 18:00 after a human approved. Overnight that is ~480 firings. Worse, `_prune_job_history` keeps the most recent 100 JobRuns, so at one skip per minute THE RECORD OF THE FIRINGS THAT DID REAL WORK IS DELETED AFTER 100 MINUTES - the loop's idling destroys the evidence of its own work. The skipping itself is CORRECT (`_loop_stall_reason` argues stopping would be unrecoverable); do not 'fix' that. See the pre-authorised direction in decisions_for_user[1].

method_reminders: A SPEC LOOP is explore+propose -> review -> review -> implement. Rounds 2 and 3 each independently compare the proposal to the actual code and FIX the proposal. It has found a real defect on four consecutive outings.
Finding defects IS the goal tonight. A sweep that finds nothing has failed, not succeeded. Do not tidy the sweep into a success story.
Every fix carries a test you RAN and WATCHED FAIL without the fix. Mutation-check guards: break the line deliberately and confirm a NAMED test fails.

Targeted per-phase test runs are NOT enough when you touch a migration - run the files that assert the head revision too (test_migrations.py, test_project_persistence.py, test_task_workspace_scheme.py).
The Hub suite takes 14-24 minutes and exceeds the 600s command cap - run it in file chunks or in the background. Do not poll it.
`cd` PERSISTS across Bash calls. Use absolute paths after any cd, or you will run commands in the wrong directory and be told 'no such file'.

The openspec validator reads ONLY THE FIRST PHYSICAL LINE of a requirement for the SHALL/MUST modal. A requirement whose SHALL falls to line 2 fails validation with a confusing error. Measured this evening.
`POST /projects` does not exist - it is POST /projects/open with {"path": ...}. PATCH /projects/{id} is a 405; settings are PUT /projects/{id}/settings.
An ALLOW is recorded nowhere - record_permission_decision persists only refusals. Never infer 'the approver did not run' from an absence of rows. That inference cost three investigations of F52.
ruff is not on PATH in Git Bash - use `py -3.11 -m ruff`. black needs --target-version py311. CI lints src/ hub/ tests/ and blacks src/ hub/hub/ hub/tests/ tests/.
A bash heredoc mangles document prose containing backticks and quotes. Write files with a Python script or the Write tool instead.
CI triggers only on push to master and PRs to it. Your feature branch gets no CI, ever - so the suites you run yourself are the only gate you have.
